evidence.title: Laas Geel Rockshelters (Hargeisa Plateau, Somaliland): Mid-Holocene Cattle Art
evidence.dateBasis: Radiometric & stylistic parallels for Saharan-Horn pastoral rock art
evidence.summary: Polychrome rockshelters preserving humpless longhorn cattle adorned with plastrons alongside pastoralists and domestic dogs above seasonal wadis.
evidence.limits: Direct pigment radiocarbon dating remains sparse; dates anchor primarily via stylistic and excavated pastoral horizons.

evidence.title: Dhambalin Sandstone Gallery (Sahil, Somaliland): Early Pastoral Hunting & Herding
evidence.dateBasis: Rock-art motif stratigraphy & Red Sea littoral survey
evidence.summary: Open sandstone alcove depicting horned cattle, sheep/goats, giraffes, and bow-equipped hunters in Ethiopian-Arabian style across coastal foothills.
evidence.limits: Sub-surface excavation adjacent to shelters remains less extensive than surface documentation.

evidence.title: Karin Hegane & Qombo’ul Coastal Caves (Sanaag, Northern Somalia)
evidence.dateBasis: Coastal survey & maritime shell midden chronology
evidence.summary: Painted caves and coastal cairns along the Gulf of Aden documenting early frankincense–incense littoral mobile herders trading near Cape Guardafui.
evidence.limits: Few high-precision AMS runs exist for Sanaag rockshelter floors.

evidence.title: Xiis (Mundus) & Xaafuun (Opone): Classical Red Sea–Indian Ocean Emporia
evidence.dateBasis: Imported Mediterranean terra sigillata, Nabataean–Parthian glazes & Periplus topography
evidence.summary: Ancient spice-and-glass entrepôts matching Classical Periplus anchorages, yielding Roman, Mediterranean, Persian, and South Arabian ceramics beside cairn burials.
evidence.limits: Monsoon wind-blown sand and scarce fresh excavation constrain continuous stratigraphic sequences.

evidence.title: Aw Barkhadle & Tiya-Style Stele Fields (Hargeisa–Berbera Corridor)
evidence.dateBasis: Islamic burial stelae epigraphy & Adal pilgrim center surveys
evidence.summary: Historic pilgrimage tomb and surrounding megalithic stone-slab field blending pre-Islamic stelae traditions with medieval Horn Islam.
evidence.limits: Chronology spans long overlapping burial episodes across pastoral and Adal-era communities.

evidence.title: Zayla (Saylac) & Saad ad-Din Island Coral Port (Somaliland)
evidence.dateBasis: Coral-rag mosque architecture, celadon sherds & Adal Sultanate chronicles
evidence.summary: Chief Red Sea port of the medieval Ifat and Adal Sultanates, linking highland Harar, Shewa leather, and Arabian–Chinese ceramic imports.
evidence.limits: Marine erosion and historic storm surges obscure lower medieval harbor quays.

evidence.title: Harlaa Cosmopolitan Entrepôt (Dire Dawa, Eastern Ethiopia)
evidence.dateBasis: Calibrated AMS charcoal dating & excavated Islamic bead-glass workshops
evidence.summary: Terraced stone trade town yielding Chinese celadon, Red Sea coinage, carnelian and glass workshop debris bridging Christian highland Ethiopia and Red Sea ports.
evidence.limits: Multi-phase masonry compounds remain under ongoing excavation outside the central mosque sector.

evidence.title: Benadir Coast Stone Ports: Mogadishu (Shangaani), Merka & Barawa
evidence.dateBasis: Dated Fakhr al-Din mosque inscriptions (1269 CE), coral arches & Kilwa-style currency
evidence.summary: Urban Indian Ocean textile-weaving and coral-stone ports hosting medieval traveler Ibn Battuta, Ming fleet contact, and inland Shabelle cotton production.
evidence.limits: Active historic neighborhoods limit deep basement trenching in central quarters.

evidence.title: Konso Basalt Agricultural Terraces & Walled Settlements (Southern Ethiopia)
evidence.dateBasis: Basalt dry-stone terrace sequences & ancestral waka stele traditions
evidence.summary: Multi-kilometer basalt retaining walls, walled ridge towns (paletas), and carved wooden waka memorials sustaining dense dryland highland farming.
evidence.limits: Radiocarbon bracketing of early terrace walls covers broader multi-century intervals.

evidence.title: Tiya & Soddo Carved Megalithic Stelae (Central Rift Highlands, Ethiopia)
evidence.dateBasis: AMS radiocarbon dates on associated burial skeletons & obsidian microliths
evidence.summary: Lines of upright basaltic stelae incised with swords and cryptic forked motifs marking elite medieval highland cemeteries along the Awash-Rift watershed.
evidence.limits: Symbolic sword icons remain open to varied social-status and clan-emblem interpretations.

evidence.title: Tsodilo Hills White Paintings & Depression Shelters (Ngamiland, Botswana)
evidence.dateBasis: Stratified quartz microlithic levels, ostrich eggshell AMS & specularite mines
evidence.summary: Sacred quartzite inselbergs holding >4,500 rock paintings, deep Middle–Later Stone Age deposits, Early Iron Age Divuyu villages, and Chobe fishbone middens.
evidence.limits: Sub-surface mixing in sandy shelter floors occasionally blurs transitional Stone-to-Iron horizons.

evidence.title: Divuyu & Nqoma Specularite–Copper Villages (Tsodilo, NW Botswana)
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon-dated Bantu-speaking agropastoralist village middens & brass jewelry
evidence.summary: Hilltop Early Iron Age farming and metallurgical settlements quarrying lustrous red specularite ore and exchanging Katanga copper and glass beads.
evidence.limits: Represents elevated specialist hilltop settlements tied to wider Okavango-Zambezi networks.

evidence.title: Toteng Early Pastoralist Horizon (Lake Ngami Basin, Botswana)
evidence.dateBasis: Direct AMS dates on Bambata pottery, sheep/cattle bone & charred seeds
evidence.summary: Kalahari lake-margin camps preserving the earliest securely dated domestic cattle and sheep remains arriving south of the Zambezi alongside LSA foraging tools.
evidence.limits: Caliche floodplain carbonates require strict bone collagen pretreatment.

evidence.title: Ga-Mohana, Khutse & Middle Kalahari Paleolake Pan Shelters (Botswana)
evidence.dateBasis: OSL-dated pan lunettes, crystal quartz microliths & paleo-wetland cores
evidence.summary: Ephemeral fossil pan and dolomitic hill occupation horizons proving continuous interior Kalahari stone-tool foraging through arid-wet Holocene shifts.
evidence.limits: Thin surface scatters around seasonal pans challenge fine stratigraphic separation.

evidence.title: Tsabong & Molopo Dryland Forager–Tswana Camps (SW Kgalagadi, Botswana)
evidence.dateBasis: Surveyed Later Stone Age lithic scatters & pastoralist ceramic associations
evidence.summary: Dry riverbed and red-dune camps tracking seasonal ostrich-eggshell water-flask caches and interaction between Khoe-San hunter-gatherers and Sotho-Tswana pastoralists.
evidence.limits: Bioturbation in aeolian Kalahari sand compresses multi-century surface assemblages.

evidence.title: Toutswemogala & Bosutswe Centralized Cattle Chiefdoms (Eastern Botswana)
evidence.dateBasis: Vitrified cattle-dung middens, Zhizo ceramics & Shashe-Limpopo glass beads
evidence.summary: Hilltop-and-plateau settlement hierarchy supported by massive vitrified kraal middens, pre-dating Mapungubwe along the eastern Kalahari fringe.
evidence.limits: Radiocarbon plateau across 1050–1250 CE widens exact abandonment estimates.

evidence.title: Twyfelfontein (/Ui-//aes) Sandstone Petroglyphs (Kunene, Namibia)
evidence.dateBasis: Desert-varnish engraving superpositioning & nearby Later Stone Age shelter levels
evidence.summary: Over 2,500 pecked engravings of rhino, giraffe, ostrich, and human-animal tracks beside permanent Aba-Huab waterholes used by desert hunter-foragers.
evidence.limits: Direct desert-varnish chronometry yields broad age brackets compared to excavated shelter charcoal.

evidence.title: Brandberg / Dâures Massive (Erongo, Namibia): Maack Shelter & Hungorob Ravine
evidence.dateBasis: Excavated stone rings, radiocarbon hearth layers & 43,000 documented paintings
evidence.summary: Granite mountain massif holding tens of thousands of fine monochrome-polychrome paintings, stone rainwater cisterns, and pastoral transitional camp huts.
evidence.limits: Direct paint radiocarbon sampling remains restricted by mineral binder compositions.

evidence.title: Geduld & Mirabib Namib Desert Shelter Sequences (Erongo/Namib)
evidence.dateBasis: Charred nara melon seeds, early pottery, sheep dung layers & ostrich-egg beads
evidence.summary: Arid Namib inselberg shelters charting long-term adaptation to Fog-belt nara melons and the 2,000-year transition to ceramic-using sheep pastoralism.
evidence.limits: Low sedimentation rates compress millennia of arid-zone occupation into shallow ash deposits.

evidence.title: Charé & Huns Mountains Holocene Shelters (Southern Namibia)
evidence.dateBasis: AMS charcoal horizons, Wilton backed microliths & early sheep-herder ceramics
evidence.summary: Orange-Fish basin escarpment rockshelters documenting Holocene Wilton hunter-gatherers and late arrival of Khoe ceramic herding groups.
evidence.limits: Later colonial pastoral grazing disturbed upper topsoil horizons at lower talus slopes.

evidence.title: Bhimbetka & Vindhya Painted Quartzite Shelters (Madhya Pradesh)
evidence.dateBasis: Mesolithic geometric microlith excavations & superimposed hematitic hunting scenes
evidence.summary: Extensive central Indian sandstone galleries overlaying stratified Acheulian and Mesolithic floors showing bow-hunting, honey-gathering, and early chalcolithic horsemen.
evidence.limits: Paint pigments without organic binders rely on archaeological floor correlation rather than direct AMS.

evidence.title: Northeastern Vindhya & Belan-Son Megalithic Cemeteries (UP–MP)
evidence.dateBasis: GIS cemetery alignments, Iron Age black-and-red ware & thermoluminescence
evidence.summary: Cairn circles and dolmenoid cists overlooking upland stream divides, tracking iron-using pastoralist-agrarian communities moving out of the Vindhya fringe.
evidence.limits: Looted or plowed central cists limit undisturbed articulated skeletal finds.

evidence.title: Vidarbha Iron Age Megaliths: Naikund & Mahurjhari (Maharashtra)
evidence.dateBasis: Excavated iron-smelting furnace tuyeres, horse-bit burials & copper bells
evidence.summary: Hundreds of stone-circle burials preserving crucible steel blades, ornamental copper-sheet horse tack, and intact iron-smelting bloomery furnaces.
evidence.limits: Acidic black-cotton soils erode softer unburned grave goods.

evidence.title: Inamgaon & Daimabad Jorwe Agrarian Villages (Bhima–Godavari Basin)
evidence.dateBasis: Excavated circular wattle-and-daub granaries, diversion canals & painted Jorwe pottery
evidence.summary: Late Deccan Chalcolithic chiefdom towns managing winter barley-wheat crop rotation through artificial river irrigation channels.
evidence.limits: Abandonment c. 700 BCE tracks regional monsoon weakening toward pastoral mobility.

evidence.title: Sisupalgarh Fortified Metropolis (Bhubaneswar, Odisha)
evidence.dateBasis: Monumental laterite-block ramparts, geophysical magnetometry & OSL strata
evidence.summary: Massive square Mauryan–Chedi planned capital in Kalinga linked with Kharavela inscriptions, rouletted fine wares, and continuous lateral urban shifts over 3,000 years.
evidence.limits: Suburban waterlogged rice paddies complicate deep trenching outside citadel gates.

evidence.title: Kalinga Littoral Temples & Palur–Manikpatna Ports (Coastal Odisha)
evidence.dateBasis: Excavated amphora-rouletted port strata, Konark chloritic stone masonry & epigraphy
evidence.summary: Mahanadi–Chilika maritime ports linking Eastern Ganga stone temples (Puri, Bhubaneswar, Konark) directly with Sri Lanka and Southeast Asian Suvarnabhumi voyages.
evidence.limits: Dynamic Chilika sandbar progradation reoriented harbor entrances every few centuries.

evidence.title: Amaravati & Nagarjunakonda Stupa Cities (Krishna River, Andhra)
evidence.dateBasis: Ikshvaku Sanskrit–Prakrit pillar inscriptions, Roman coin hoards & limestone reliefs
evidence.summary: Satavahana and Ikshvaku Buddhist monastic universities and brick amphitheaters lining the Krishna River trade corridor between Deccan interiors and eastern sea ports.
evidence.limits: Lower Nagarjunakonda structures survive today partly reconstructed above reservoir waters.

evidence.title: Ajanta, Ellora & Badami Basalt Rock-Cut Monasteries (Maharashtra–Karnataka)
evidence.dateBasis: Vakataka, Chalukya & Rashtrakuta temple inscriptions & mineral temper paintings
evidence.summary: Monolithic basalt sanctuaries (including Kailasa excavated top-down from cliffs) serving simultaneously Buddhist viharas, Hindu temples, and Jain basadis along Sahyadri passes.
evidence.limits: Chronological overlap between early Hinayana and Vakataka patronage relies on palaeography.

evidence.title: Adichanallur, Keeladi & Hire Benakal South Indian Iron–Urban Sequence
evidence.dateBasis: AMS charred paddy grains, Tamil-Brahmi graffitied sherds & dolmen granite slabs
evidence.summary: Dense dolmen megaliths across Tungabhadra–Vaigai–Tamiraparani valleys transitioning into iron-rich industrial urban quarters with high-tin bronze vessels and Tamil-Brahmi script.
evidence.limits: Urn-burial acid soils limit DNA retrieval across humid southern sectors.

evidence.title: Rajgir–Nalanda–Patna Magadhan Heartland (Central Ganges, Bihar)
evidence.dateBasis: NBPW stratigraphy, Cyclone cyclopean rubble walls & Nalanda copper-plate seals
evidence.summary: Iron-rich urban core of Magadha, Mauryan Pataliputra palisades, and the residential Mahavihara university of Nalanda teaching astronomy, logic, and medicine to pilgrims across Asia.
evidence.limits: High alluvial groundwater tables block deep pre-Mauryan excavations beneath modern Patna.

evidence.title: Digaru–Kolong Valley & Assam–Meghalaya Foothills (Assam, India)
evidence.dateBasis: Recent AMS radiocarbon dates on cord-impressed Neolithic–early historic pottery
evidence.summary: Shouldered basalt celts, cord-marked stoneware, and brick temple foundations anchoring Neolithic and early state networks across the southern Brahmaputra valley.
evidence.limits: Acidic lateritic soils and monsoon erosion restrict fragile bone preservation.

evidence.title: Nartiang & Khasi–Jaintia Monolithic Grounds (Meghalaya, India)
evidence.dateBasis: Oral clan chronologies, sandstone menhir–dolmen avenues & ethnographic records
evidence.summary: Forests of towering upright sandstone menhirs (up to 8 m) and horizontal table-stones erected by Jaintia and Khasi matrilineal clans for market shrines and ancestral memorials.
evidence.limits: Few organic foundation samples permit tight single-century radiocarbon bracketing.

evidence.title: Ambari Urban Quarter & Kamarupa Brick Temples (Guwahati, Brahmaputra)
evidence.dateBasis: Kaolin pottery sequences, stone sculpture caches & Chinese celadon sherds
evidence.summary: Submerged urban workshop center of Kamarupa revealing green kaolin pottery, copper-plate land grants, and Himalayan–Tibetan silk transit routes.
evidence.limits: Deep urban construction limits horizontal area exposure.

evidence.title: Charaideo Maidams & Ahom Hydraulic Kingdom (Upper Assam)
evidence.dateBasis: Assam Buranji chronicles, octagonal brick-vaulted burial tumuli & stone reservoirs
evidence.summary: Upper Brahmaputra royal capital founded by Tai-Ahom migrants, integrating monumental earthen-and-brick tumuli (maidams), wet-rice bunds, and multi-ethnic frontier statecraft.
evidence.limits: Excavation inside sacred royal vaults remains sensitively limited.

evidence.title: Wari-Bateshwar & Mahasthangarh (Old Brahmaputra–Karatoa Delta, Bangladesh)
evidence.dateBasis: AMS charcoal dates, punch-marked silver coins, semi-precious bead kilns & NBPW
evidence.summary: Walled Delta fort cities (Pundranagara) manufacturing etched carnelian, glass beads, and high-tin bronzes linking Bengal river highways with overland silk passes.
evidence.limits: Periodic river avulsion shifts older alluvial channels away from brick citadels.

evidence.title: Paharpur Somapura Mahavihara & Mainamati Brick Monasteries (Bangladesh)
evidence.dateBasis: Pala clay-brick terracotta plaques, Devaparvata copper plates & Tibetan accounts
evidence.summary: Monumental terraced brick Buddhist cruciform stupa complexes patronized by Pala and Chandra kings, mentoring Southeast Asian brick architecture (Pagan, Prambanan).
evidence.limits: Delta humidity and saline capillary rise challenge soft carved terracotta friezes.

evidence.title: Nyaunggan & Oakaie Late Neolithic–Early Bronze Cemeteries (Chindwin, Myanmar)
evidence.dateBasis: Multi-lab AMS human-tooth and charcoal chronology with lead-isotope bronze matching
evidence.summary: Excavated graves demonstrating dry-zone copper-bronze socketed axes, jadeite rings, and inland agro-pastoral villages along the Chindwin valley by ~1000–800 BCE.
evidence.limits: High alkalinity in dry-zone sands impacts collagen yield outside tooth enamel.

evidence.title: Halin, Beikthano & Sri Ksetra Walled Pyu Hydraulic Cities (Irrawaddy, Myanmar)
evidence.dateBasis: Elliptical brick ramparts, Pyu–Brahmi inscribed urns & brick reservoir dams
evidence.summary: Early Tibeto-Burman brick-walled irrigated cities building towering cylindrical stupas (Bawbawgyi) and silver coinage centuries before Bagan unified the Irrawaddy.
evidence.limits: Early 20th-century trenching disturbed several inner brick monastery fills.

evidence.title: Bagan Monumental Brick Plain (Mandalay Region, Myanmar)
evidence.dateBasis: Over 2,000 surviving brick stupas, Myazedi multilingual inscription (1113 CE) & murals
evidence.summary: Anawrahta and Kyanzittha’s imperial capital spanning a dry-zone plain of >3,000 Buddhist brick temples, irrigation canals, and Mon–Pyu–Burmese–Pali scholarship.
evidence.limits: Seismic vulnerability (1975, 2016) obscures upper stucco stratigraphy.

evidence.title: Mrauk U Coastal Fortress Kingdom (Rakhine Coast, Myanmar)
evidence.dateBasis: Sandstone labyrinthine Shitthaung temple carvings & Bay of Bengal Portuguese records
evidence.summary: River-diked stone citadel kingdom linking Arakanese rice plains, Bengal Sultanate court scripts, Japanese/Dutch mercenaries, and Bay of Bengal coastal maritime trade.
evidence.limits: Isolated Rakhine coastal access limits modern geophysical prospection.

evidence.title: Lakaton’i Anja Rockshelter & Northern Earliest Madagascar Foragers (Antsiranana)
evidence.dateBasis: OSL sediment & AMS bone/charcoal dates alongside imported chert-glass beads
evidence.summary: Calcareous shelter in northern Madagascar preserving controversial early stone microliths and foraging debris, framing debates over pre-Austronesian visits vs Holocene timing.
evidence.limits: Stratigraphic disturbance and rare 1st-millennium BCE OSL ages remain actively debated in Island archaeology.

evidence.title: Dembeni (Mayotte, Comoros) & Transoceanic Asian–Bantu Botanical Nexus
evidence.dateBasis: Flotation of charred Asian rice, mung bean & African sorghum/pearl millet grains
evidence.summary: Hilltop-and-coastal Swahili/Comorian town providing earliest unequivocal botanical proof of combined African savanna crops and Southeast Asian cultivars crossing the Indian Ocean.
evidence.limits: Island deforestation terraces eroded portions of upper early-second-millennium deposits.

evidence.title: Mahilaka Walled Indian Ocean Port (Ampasindava Bay, NW Madagascar)
evidence.dateBasis: Coral-stone fortresses, chlorite-schist turned stone bowls & Sasanian-Chinese glazes
evidence.summary: Early Malagasy urban port enclosing residential quarters, crystal quartz workshops, and iron furnaces linked directly into Kilwa–Persian Gulf Swahili trade.
evidence.limits: Dense coastal coconut plantations cover peripheral artisanal sectors.

evidence.title: Vohemar (Iharana) & Northeast Chlorite-Schist Necropolis Coast
evidence.dateBasis: Excavated stone quarries, three-legged schist cooking pots & Ming blue-and-white bowls
evidence.summary: Northeastern Malagasy coastal craft communities exporting carved fire-resistant chlorite-schist tripods along the western Indian Ocean corridor.
evidence.limits: Older colonial cemetery excavations mixed grave contexts before modern provenance recovery.

evidence.title: Teniky Carved Sandstone Cliff Complex (Isalo Massif, Southern Madagascar)
evidence.dateBasis: Calibrated radiocarbon dates, carved rock niches & rare medieval West/SE Asian parallels
evidence.summary: Remote canyon sanctuary featuring dry-stone terraces and geometric cliff-cut rock cavities whose distinctive stoneworking lacks clear regional Malagasy parallels.
evidence.limits: Purpose (burial caves, trade retreat, or esoteric cult) remains under active archaeological investigation.

evidence.title: Andaro & Androy Dryland Spiny-Forest Pastoral Settlements (South Madagascar)
evidence.dateBasis: Sub-fossil elephant-bird eggshell AMS runs, clay pots & dryland zebu kraals
evidence.summary: Arid southern stone-and-thorn villages showing coexistence and final disappearance of Aepyornis giant birds alongside cattle pastoralism.
evidence.limits: Surface eggshell scatters can mix dates across wind-deflated sandy deflation pans.

evidence.title: Imerina Vohitra Fortified Ditch Villages (Central Madagascar Highlands)
evidence.dateBasis: Excavated hadivory deep concentric moats & highland paddy irrigation basins
evidence.summary: Highland hill-top earthworks encircled by massive defensive ditches and fig-grove gates preceding the unified 1790s Merina state.
evidence.limits: Later Merina stone gateway rebuilding overlays earliest mud-moat earthen ramparts.

evidence.title: Anjiro & East Coast Forest–Sea Horizons (Toamasina–Antongil Corridor)
evidence.dateBasis: Flotation of rice, yams & taro phytoliths with littoral iron-slag middens
evidence.summary: Wet tropical east coast landing corridor where Austronesian outrigger maritime technology took root with taro, bananas, and upland hill-rice swidden systems.
evidence.limits: Intense cyclonic rainfall rapidly dissolves organic bone and fragile low-fired pottery.

evidence.title: Odai Yamamoto I & Incipient Jōmon Hearth Ceramics (Aomori, Honshu)
evidence.dateBasis: AMS radiocarbon dates on carbonized cooking residue adhering to flat-bottomed sherds
evidence.summary: Among the world’s earliest ceramic cooking pots, fired by mobile Terminal Pleistocene foragers in northern Honshu around 14,500 BCE to boil aquatic and forest foods.
evidence.limits: Small assemblage size reflects seasonal short-term hunting camps.

evidence.title: Uenohara & Southern Kyushu Early Jōmon Pit-House Villages (Kagoshima)
evidence.dateBasis: Tephra Kikai-Akahoya volcanic ash marker beds & pit-hearth radiocarbon runs
evidence.summary: Sedentary early Holocene acorn-processing villages with paired smoke-tunnels, lacquered wooden bowls, and ceramic figurines flourishing prior to the 7.3 ka Kikai caldera eruption.
evidence.limits: Akahoya pumice fall cleanly caps pre-5300 BCE floors before millennia of depopulation.

evidence.title: Sannai-Maruyama Great Chestnut Village (Aomori, Northern Japan)
evidence.dateBasis: DNA chestnut-pollen spectra, six-pillar giant timber postholes & jadeite ornaments
evidence.summary: Long-lived Jōmon central settlement featuring managed chestnut groves, giant chestnut-pillar monuments, longhouses, and Itoigawa jadeite trade across Honshu.
evidence.limits: Late Middle Jōmon cooling coincided with sudden abandonment of monumental pit clusters.

evidence.title: Kitakogane Shell Mounds & Hokkaido Jōmon Maritime Adaptations
evidence.dateBasis: Salmon-bone stable isotopes, whale-bone harpoons & clay-figurine mounds
evidence.summary: Northern maritime Jōmon communities sustaining dense year-round settlements on Pacific shellfish, fur seals, salmon runs, and Hokkaido obsidian exchanges.
evidence.limits: Cold coastal soils dissolve uncalcined wooden nets and boats outside waterlogged sites.

evidence.title: Itazuke & Nabatake Earliest Wet-Rice Yayoi Fields (Northern Kyushu)
evidence.dateBasis: AMS charred rice grains, wooden sluice gates, bronze weapons & Kyushu aDNA
evidence.summary: Irrigated rice paddy ditches with crescent stone harvesting knives and Mumun-style pottery demonstrating early continental agricultural migration into Kyushu.
evidence.limits: Early onset dates around 900–800 BCE resolved earlier Yayoi calibration debates.

evidence.title: Yoshinogari Moated Yayoi Confederated Town (Saga, Kyushu)
evidence.dateBasis: Double V-ditch defensive moats, raised granaries, watchtowers & bronze mirrors
evidence.summary: Fortified 40-hectare Yayoi regional center matching Chinese Wei Chronicles accounts of ranked Wa confederations, silk weaving, and thousands of jar burials.
evidence.limits: Watchtower reconstructions model posthole dimensions rather than intact upper joinery.

evidence.title: Toro Waterlogged Yayoi Paddy–Village Complex (Shizuoka, Central Honshu)
evidence.dateBasis: Dendrochronology on cedar paddy planks, raised-floor storehouses & wooden spades
evidence.summary: Exceptionally waterlogged Suruga Bay settlement preserving intact wooden paddy embankments, geta clogs, fire-drills, and elevated rat-proof rice storehouses.
evidence.limits: Flood burial sealed the residential sector abruptly around 300 CE.

evidence.title: Mozu–Furuichi Giant Keyhole Kofun Mounds (Osaka–Sakai Plains)
evidence.dateBasis: Ceramic Sue ware typologies, haniwa terracotta guardians & imperial tomb chronologies
evidence.summary: Over a hundred monumental keyhole-shaped earthen royal tombs (up to 486 m long), channeling Yamato basin corvée labor and Baekje ironworking immigration.
evidence.limits: Strict Imperial Household Agency protection bars intrusive digging of central royal chambers.

evidence.title: Asuka & Heijō-kyō (Nara): First Permanent Grid Capital & Daibutsu Bronze
evidence.dateBasis: Excavated wooden mokkan tax slips, Tang-style grid streets & Todai-ji bronze
evidence.summary: Seat of Nara state Buddhism and ritsuryō administration where hundreds of thousands of inscribed wooden mokkan documents track province-wide tax salt, cloth, and rice shipments.
evidence.limits: Capital relocated abruptly north to Nagaoka and Kyoto in 784–794 CE.

evidence.title: Epi-Jōmon & Okhotsk Maritime Seal Hunters (Rishiri–Shiretoko, Hokkaido)
evidence.dateBasis: Marine-mammal harpoons, bone needle cases & Amur-Sakhalin iron trade wares
evidence.summary: Distinct Sea-of-Okhotsk coastal culture thriving along northern Hokkaido and the Kurils on Steller sea lion hunting, bear ritual, and Amur metal imports before Satsumon/Ainu fusion.
evidence.limits: Acidic volcanic soils outside shell middens degrade fragile wood.

evidence.title: Hiraizumi Buddhist Gardens & Northern Gold-Horse Frontier (Iwate)
evidence.dateBasis: Gold-leaf Konjikidō hall, Pure Land pond gardens & Yanagi no Gosho palace trenches
evidence.summary: Wealthy northern Oshu Fujiwara court funding gold-leaf Pure Land temples through Kitakami gold dust, northern warhorse breeding, and Hokkaido sea-otter/kelp exchange.
evidence.limits: Toppled militarily by Minamoto no Yoritomo in 1189 CE.

evidence.title: Kamakura Waterfront, Tsurugaoka & Wakaejima Stone Jetty (Kanagawa)
evidence.dateBasis: Excavated Song-Yuan ceramic beaches, basalt jetty boulders & shogunal Azuma Kagami
evidence.summary: Coastal military shogunate capital boxed by steep pass fortifications (kiridoshi), hosting Zen monasteries and Japan’s oldest surviving artificial stone harbor pier.
evidence.limits: Modern dense housing covers most medieval samurai residential lots.

evidence.title: Amsa-dong Comb-Patterned Village (Han River, Seoul, South Korea)
evidence.dateBasis: AMS acorn/hearth dates & semi-subterranean Jeulmun pit houses
evidence.summary: Neolithic Han River fishing, acorn-leaching, and wild-millet pit village typified by pointed-base comb-marked Jeulmun earthenware vessels.
evidence.limits: Flooding silts preserved sunken house floors better than perishable organic nets.

evidence.title: Songguk-ri Mumun Dryfield–Paddy Settlement (Buyeo, Chungnam, South Korea)
evidence.dateBasis: Carbonized rice/millet grains, lipid residue & Liaoning-type bronze daggers
evidence.summary: Canonical Middle Mumun ranked farming village with distinctive round central-trench houses, stone semilunar reaping knives, and greenstone tubular beads.
evidence.limits: Chronology anchors directly into early wet-rice diffusion toward Kyushu.

evidence.title: Gochang, Hwasun & Ganghwa Bronze Age Dolmen Cemeteries (South Korea)
evidence.dateBasis: Multi-ton capstones, bronze daggers, red-burnished pottery & Mumun radiocarbon runs
evidence.summary: Tens of thousands of massive granite northern-table and southern-go-table megalithic chamber tombs demonstrating dense Bronze Age lineage monumentality across Korea.
evidence.limits: Many capstones sit above looted or acid-leached skeletal chambers.

evidence.title: Ji’an Mountain Citadels & Goguryeo Painted Murals (Yalu River Basin)
evidence.dateBasis: Inscribed Gwanggaeto Stele (414 CE), Guonei stone fortress & frescoed stone chambers
evidence.summary: Steppe-and-mountain cavalry kingdom along the middle Yalu building granite cliff fortresses (Hwando) and vivid tomb murals of astronomy, wrestling, and armored horsemen.
evidence.limits: Sino-Korean border division partitions Ji’an (Jilin) and Pyongyang capitals across modern frontiers.

evidence.title: Gyeongju (Seorabeol): Golden Silla Royal Tombs, Hwangnyongsa & Cheomseongdae
evidence.dateBasis: Wood-chamber mound stratigraphy, golden shaman-style crowns & Sasanian Roman glass
evidence.summary: Southeastern Korean kingdom capital housing monumental river-cobble tumuli packed with gold granulation crowns, jade commas, Central Asian glass vessels, and East Asia’s oldest stone observatory.
evidence.limits: Monumental Cheonmachong/Hwangnam mounds contrast with sparsely excavated commoner wards.

evidence.title: Gongju & Buyeo Baekje Capitals: Mireuksa & Maritime Silk Exchange
evidence.dateBasis: Mireuksa gold-relic box inscriptions (639 CE), gilt-bronze incense burners & kilns
evidence.summary: Southwestern Korean maritime kingdom diffusing Buddhist architecture, gilded bronze metallurgy, Confucian scholarship, and irrigation engineering across the Yellow Sea to Yamato Japan.
evidence.limits: Wooden palaces burned in 660 CE leaving granite podiums and celadon roof tiles.

evidence.title: Daegaya & Geumgwan Gaya Iron-Smelting Confederacies (Nakdong Delta)
evidence.dateBasis: Excavated iron-ingot plate armor, shell mounds & Nakdong coastal kiln strata
evidence.summary: Maritime river-mouth confederacy exporting flat iron bars (cheoljeong), horse armor, and high-fired stoneware bowls between China, Silla, and Kyushu.
evidence.limits: Rapid urbanization around modern Busan/Gimhae overlays delta harbor middens.

evidence.title: Niuheliang Hongshan Jade & Goddess Temple Center (Western Liaoning)
evidence.dateBasis: AMS bones, coiled nephrite pig-dragons & subterranean painted mud-plaster shrines
evidence.summary: Neolithic ceremonial ridge complex across Liaoning Manchuria producing fine coiled green nephrite jades, sculpted life-size goddess busts, and stepped stone-cairn altars.
evidence.limits: Limited domestic habitation excavations leave ceremonial population mobility unclear.

evidence.title: Balhae / Bohai Upper Capital Shangjing & Mudan River Plain (Heilongjiang)
evidence.dateBasis: Basalt palace terraces, underfloor heated kang flues, Korean-Tang ceramics & annals
evidence.summary: Multi-ethnic Goguryeo–Mohe northern kingdom ("Flourishing Kingdom of the East") combining Tang imperial grid boulevards with sub-zero kang heated palace floors.
evidence.limits: Destroyed by Khitan Liao conquests in 926 CE.

evidence.title: Jurchen Jin Upper Capital & Early Manchu Hetu Ala / Mukden (Liaoning)
evidence.dateBasis: Eight-Banner military registers, stone fortresses & octagonal Dazheng Hall architecture
evidence.summary: Tungusic Jurchen and Manchu homeland linking sable-hunting and ginseng tributaries of the Liao-Amur forests into northern China’s Jurchen Jin and later Qing state.
evidence.limits: Seventeenth-century imperial palace renovations at Mukden post-date initial Nurhaci hill-forts.

evidence.title: Bosumpra (Kwahu, Ghana) & Shum Laka Late Pleistocene–Holocene Forest Shelters
evidence.dateBasis: Quartz microliths, ground celts, pearl millet-oil palm macrobotanicals & AMS dates
evidence.summary: Primary closed-forest escarpment rockshelters tracing human transition from quartz microlithic hunter-foragers to oil-palm arboriculture and early Kintampo village potteries.
evidence.limits: Warm humid rainforest soils rarely preserve uncharred macrofaunal bones.

evidence.title: Bonoase & Kintampo Ceramic–Oil Palm Settled Villages (Ghana Forest Fringe)
evidence.dateBasis: Direct AMS on pearl millet (Pennisetum) & stamped terracotta rasps
evidence.summary: Earliest settled food-producing villages across the Ghanaian savanna-forest transition combining Sahelian pearl millet, oil palm, dwarf goats, and wattle-and-daub huts.
evidence.limits: Terracotta "cigars" remain enigmatic in exact economic or ritual purpose.

evidence.title: Ile-Ife Glass Bead Crucibles, Terracotta Art & Potsherd Pavements (Nigeria)
evidence.dateBasis: TL-dated herring-bone potsherd courtyards, HLHA glass crucibles & medieval cotton/wheat
evidence.summary: Sacred Yoruba forest metropolis synthesizing primary glass production (high-lime high-alumina glass), naturalistically modeled brass/terracotta heads, and Saharan cotton/wheat ties.
evidence.limits: Modern dense city blocks cap large portions of medieval pavement precincts.

evidence.title: Igbo-Ukwu Igbo forest Sanctuary: Lost-Wax Copper-Lead Shrines (Anambra, Nigeria)
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon wooden-plank tombs, leaded-bronze roped vessels & 165,000 glass beads
evidence.summary: Southeastern Nigerian rainforest ritual storehouses and royal burial yielding extraordinary lost-wax leaded-bronze roped vessels cast centuries before European coastal contact.
evidence.limits: Local copper-tin source provenance vs trans-Saharan glass bead origins continue active isotope study.

evidence.title: Sungbo’s Eredo & Ijebu 160-km Rainforest Rampart Circuit (Ogun, Nigeria)
evidence.dateBasis: AMS charcoal buried beneath ditch-and-bank embankments & optical lidar traverses
evidence.summary: Colossal 160-kilometer continuous earthen rampart and steep ditch encircling the Ijebu forest kingdom east of Lagos, mobilizing immense organized forest labor.
evidence.limits: Multiple repair episodes across centuries complicate single-construction chronology.

evidence.title: Begho & Bono Manso Brong Forest-Edge Gold-Kola Entrepôts (Ghana)
evidence.dateBasis: Excavated Dyula quarter brass weights, Sahelian tobacco pipes & spun spindle whorls
evidence.summary: Twin Brong Akan towns feeding Lobi–Ashanti alluvial gold dust and forest kola nuts north along Wangara–Dyula donkey-and-porter routes toward Djenné and Timbuktu.
evidence.limits: Town displacement during 18th-century Asante wars leaves mostly flat mound fields.

evidence.title: Yengema & Sapi–Temne Soapstone Nomoli Crossroads (Sierra Leone–Guinea)
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon cave levels & coastal mangrove shell mounds along Upper Guinea
evidence.summary: Humid Upper Guinea forest-coast zone known for early stone-axe and cord-rouletted pottery alongside carved steatite ancestral figures (nomoli) traded pre-1500.
evidence.limits: Loose antiquarian finds of steatite carvings lack primary stratified context.

evidence.title: Kong & Dabakala Savanna–Forest Islamic Silk-Weaving Corridors (Côte d’Ivoire)
evidence.dateBasis: Wattara Dyula mud mosques, indigo-strip cotton markets & trade manuscripts
evidence.summary: Northern Ivorian forest-margin market city connecting kola groves of the Sassandra–Bandama rainforest directly across the Volta into Mali mosques.
evidence.limits: Destroyed largely during 1897 Samori Touré wars prior to photographic surveys.

evidence.title: Dhar Tichitt–Oualata Stone Escarpment Villages (Mauritania)
evidence.dateBasis: AMS pearl millet chaff inside potsherds & 400+ dry-stone masonry plateau towns
evidence.summary: Monumental dry-stone walled compounds perched along sandstone cliffs during Sahelian desiccation, incubating the earliest Saharan domesticated pearl millet agriculture and proto-urban chiefdoms.
evidence.limits: Shallow rocky plateaus preserve surface plans cleanly while limiting stratified midden depth.

evidence.title: Dhar Néma Late Holocene Pastoral–Iron Crossroads (SE Mauritania)
evidence.dateBasis: Stratified bone-temper sherds, bloomery iron slag & dated pearl-millet chaff
evidence.summary: Key Mauritanian frontier bridging early Tichitt farming settlements toward Sahelian iron metallurgy centuries before imperial Ghana coalesced nearby.
evidence.limits: Wind deflation strips upper Late Iron Age sandy horizons across open mounds.

evidence.title: Kumbi Saleh (Wagadu / Imperial Ghana) Stone Quarter (Mauritania)
evidence.dateBasis: Calibrated AMS dates on Columns Tomb timber & stone-slab merchant houses
evidence.summary: Twin-city urban landscape of Imperial Wagadu (Ghana) preserving multi-story schist-slab merchant mansions, painted Arabic stelae, and monumental columned tombs.
evidence.limits: Excavations focused heavily on the merchant stone town over royal Al-Ghaba timber quarters.

evidence.title: Aoudaghost (Tegdaoust) Southern Saharan Caravan Terminus (Mauritania)
evidence.dateBasis: Stratified multi-story stone ruins, brass scale weights & Fatimid glass weights
evidence.summary: Oasis entrepôt connecting southern Moroccan Sijilmasa salt-and-cloth caravans with Wagadu Bambuk goldfields before Almoravid–Malian shifts.
evidence.limits: Multiple overlapping clay-stone rebuilding campaigns complicate exact dynastic breaks.

evidence.title: Jarma (Garama) & Wadi al-Ajal Foggara Kingdoms (Fazzan, SW Libya)
evidence.dateBasis: AMS date-palm foggara shafts, subterranean irrigation canals & mudbrick forts
evidence.summary: Chariot-using Saharan Garamantian civilization digging hundreds of kilometers of subterranean foggara water channels to farm wheat, grapes, dates, and cotton across hyper-arid Libya.
evidence.limits: Pleistocene aquifer depletion over centuries left foggaras dry by Islamic transformation.

evidence.title: Sijilmasa & Wadi Ziz Tafilalt Desert Coinage City (SE Morocco)
evidence.dateBasis: Excavated rammed-earth city walls, gold dinar mint slag & river-diversion weirs
evidence.summary: Great northern gateway of medieval West African alluvial gold minted into North African and Mediterranean dinars at the edge of the Moroccan Sahara.
evidence.limits: Post-1393 destruction dispersed populations into dispersed earthen ksour.

evidence.title: Middle Draa Valley Oasis Ksour & Qanat Fields (Southern Morocco)
evidence.dateBasis: AMS charcoal in oasis soils, rammed-earth citadels (ighrem) & slag dumps
evidence.summary: Anti-Atlas Saharan oasis river ribbon sustaining fortified date-palm granaries (igoudar), irrigated barley terraces, and copper mining linking Draa to Senegal.
evidence.limits: Continuous oasis cultivation recycles older rammed-earth wall earth into newer fields.

evidence.title: M’zab Valley Underground Oasis Dams & Tassili–Hoggar Routes (Algeria)
evidence.dateBasis: Five Ibadi hilltop fortified towns (Ksar), flood-capture barrages & wells
evidence.summary: Saharan desert architectural urbanism harvesting flash-flood wadis through limestone dams and shaded market squares to sustain trans-Saharan Touggourt–Timbuktu commerce.
evidence.limits: Living heritage regulations conserve urban walls while limiting destructive foundation digging.

evidence.title: Taxila–Sirkap & Jaulian Gandharan Buddhist Universities (Punjab, Pakistan)
evidence.dateBasis: Marshall grid-street stratigraphy, silver-gold hoards & Kushan–Kidarite inscriptions
evidence.summary: Gridded Sirkap urban complex, Dharmarajika stupa, and Jaulian hillside monastery synthesizing Kushan royal patronage, Greco-Roman sculpture workshops, and Sanskrit-Prakrit learning.
evidence.limits: Ephthalite fifth-century raids ended major Gandharan monastic endowments.

evidence.title: Takht-i-Bahi Schist Ridge Monastery & Barikot Urban Continuity (KP)
evidence.dateBasis: Kushan schist stupa courts, terracotta reliefs & excavated Swat urban phases
evidence.summary: Ridge-top Buddhist monastery and Swat valley urban center illustrating multi-ethnic Kushan–Parthian–Sasanian commerce across the Khyber–Malakand passes.
evidence.limits: Older unsystematic clearings removed loose stucco heads prior to modern conservation.

evidence.title: Banbhore (Debal) Coastal Indus Port & Early Mosque (Sindh, Pakistan)
evidence.dateBasis: Excavated Scytho-Parthian basal strata, 727 CE Kufic mosque slab & glazed ceramics
evidence.summary: Indus delta harbor linking Umayyad–Abbasid Persian Gulf ships, carved ivory workshops, and Chinese stoneware until Indus channel siltation dried the creek.
evidence.limits: Coastal lagoon salinity corrodes exposed brick bases.

evidence.title: Al-Mansura & Multan Upper Indus Islamic Emirates (Sindh–Punjab)
evidence.dateBasis: Burnt-brick street plans, bronze elephant doorknockers & coin dies
evidence.summary: Planned early Islamic capitals controlling lower and middle Indus river commerce, copper coinage, and overland Multan–Ghazni caravan passes.
evidence.limits: Changing Indus meanders eroded sections of outer brick perimeter walls.

evidence.title: Uch Sharif Blue-Tile Tombs & Multan Sufi Riverine Crossroads (Punjab)
evidence.dateBasis: Lapis-cobalt glazed tilework, brick batter tombs & Ghurid–Suhrawardiyya records
evidence.summary: Chenab-Sutlej confluence religious and literary seat preserving distinctive blue-and-white Central Asian glazed tilework tombs built across river floodplains.
evidence.limits: 1817 floods undercut three major western mausolea terraces.

evidence.title: Makli Hill Necropolis & Samma–Tarkhan Thatta (Lower Indus, Sindh)
evidence.dateBasis: Carved yellow sandstone cenotaphs, glazed brickwork & Portuguese-Mughal port chronicles
evidence.summary: Vast plateau necropolis documenting lower Indus delta architecture blending Gujarati stone corbelling, Persian calligraphy, and Central Asian blue-glazed domes.
evidence.limits: Monsoon humidity and salt efflorescence challenge delicate sandstone relief carving.

evidence.title: Phùng Nguyên, Đồng Đậu & Đông Sơn Red River Bronze Sequence (Northern Vietnam)
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon wooden coffins, bronze kettle-drum alloys & Co Loa spiral citadel trenches
evidence.summary: Red River agrarian sequence rising through jade-ringed Phùng Nguyên villages into monumental cast-bronze Đông Sơn war-drums (trống đồng) and Co Loa moated earth ramparts.
evidence.limits: Waterlogged coffin burials occur sporadically across dynamic delta alluvia.

evidence.title: Sa Huỳnh Coastal Ear-Pendant & Jar-Burial Ports (Quảng Ngãi–Hội An, Vietnam)
evidence.dateBasis: AMS charcoal inside funerary jars & nephrite lingling-o isotope sourcing
evidence.summary: Coastal Austronesian iron-using mariners crafting two-headed nephrite jade earrings, carnelian beads, and bronze bowls exchanged across Taiwan, Luzon, and Thailand prior to Han expansion.
evidence.limits: Coastal sand-dune shifting leaves unexcavated burial fields scattered.

evidence.title: Ban Chiang Red-on-Buff Painted Pottery Sequence (Udon Thani, NE Thailand)
evidence.dateBasis: Bayesian AMS on rice chaff & skeletal collagen revising Bronze Age start to c. 1050 BCE
evidence.summary: Mekong plateau village mounds preserving rice-tempered grave vessels, bimetallic bronze-iron spearpoints, and distinctive swirled red-painted pottery.
evidence.limits: Early 1970s TL ages were revised significantly younger by 2010s AMS collagen programs.

evidence.title: Ban Non Wat Moated Mun Valley Neolithic–Iron Sequence (Thailand)
evidence.dateBasis: 75 Bayesian radiocarbon dates on freshwater shell, pig bone & human collagen
evidence.summary: Exceptional 640-burial Mun River village mound establishing high-precision Bayesian chronology for rice domestication (1750 BCE), copper-bronze wealth (1000 BCE), and Iron Age moats.
evidence.limits: Moated earthworks expanded dynamically during the late first millennium BCE.

evidence.title: Non Nok Tha & Phu Lon Copper Mining Highlands (Loei–Khon Kaen, Thailand)
evidence.dateBasis: Smelting crucible slags, sandstone bivalve molds & mining-pit charcoal AMS
evidence.summary: Upper Mekong sandstone-quarry and copper-mining workshops casting bronze axes and ornaments using highland ores transported to Khorat Plateau farming towns.
evidence.limits: Later iron-age re-digging occasionally mixes copper-smithing mound strata.

evidence.title: Khok Phanom Di Coastal Mangrove Pottery & Rice Complex (Chonburi, Thailand)
evidence.dateBasis: 19 radiocarbon runs across 7 m deep mangrove-estuary midden & rice sickle blades
evidence.summary: Tidal Bang Pakong estuary settlement showing extraordinary specialist female potters, shell jewelry exchange, and cyclical wetland-rice cultivation shifting with sea-level fall.
evidence.limits: Represented coastal marine focus distinct from inland Khorat plateau sites.

evidence.title: Khao Sam Kaeo Kra Isthmus Early Bead–Glass Workshop (Chumphon, Thailand)
evidence.dateBasis: AMS ironworking terraces, Indian Rouletted Ware, agate quarries & Đông Sơn drums
evidence.summary: Cosmopolitan portage town spanning fortified Kra Isthmus hills centuries before 0 CE, manufacturing etched agate, stone seals, and high-tin bronze alongside Indian and Chinese artisans.
evidence.limits: Hilltop terracotta terrace structures suffered historical treasure-hunting prior to systematic work.

evidence.title: Phum Snay & Prohear Mekong Early Iron Age Chiefdoms (Cambodia–Mekong)
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon graves, bronze horned buffalo epaulettes, agate beads & gold foil
evidence.summary: Pre-Funan Mekong and northwest Cambodian iron-age chiefdoms deploying iron swords, Indochinese bronze drums, and imported glass beads centuries before Angkor.
evidence.limits: Early road construction and looting disturbed major burial sectors prior to salvage rescue.
